drivingQuestion: What is different about wine, that a separate blessing was established for it and not for olive oil?
outcomeNote: Wine is distinguished as both satisfying and gladdening, and is exempt from the three blessings because people do not base meals on it; only the sub-dilemma of one who does base his meal on wine is left to Elijah, with a practical default in the meantime.

segments.he: אָמְרִי: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר. הֵיכִי נְבָרֵיךְ? נְבָרֵיךְ ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַזַּיִת״ — פֵּירָא גּוּפֵיהּ ״זַיִת״ אִקְּרִי.
segments.en: The Sages «said: There,» in the case of oil, «it is because it is impossible» to find an appropriate blessing, as «how shall we recite the blessing?» If «we recite the blessing: Who creates fruit of the olive, the fruit itself is called olive» and that is what was created. The oil is a man-made product of that fruit, rendering that formula inappropriate. Similarly, reciting a formula parallel to the blessing on wine: Who creates the fruit of the vine, is inappropriate as the grapes themselves are the fruit that was created, as opposed to oil which was not.

segments.he: וּנְבָרֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי עֵץ זַיִת״? אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: חַמְרָא — זָיֵין, מִשְׁחָא — לָא זָיֵין.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: Nevertheless, it is still possible to formulate a blessing, «as we may recite the blessing: Who creates fruit of the olive tree,» which would be parallel to the blessing recited over wine. «Rather, Mar Zutra offered» a different rationale: The reason that no separate blessing was established over oil is because, as opposed to «wine» that «nourishes, oil does not nourish.»

segments.he: וּמִשְׁחָא לָא זָיֵין? וְהָתְנַן הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַמָּזוֹן — מוּתָּר בַּמַּיִם וּבַמֶּלַח. וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַיִם וּמֶלַח הוּא דְּלָא אִקְּרִי ״מָזוֹן״, הָא כׇּל מִילֵּי אִקְּרִי ״מָזוֹן״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And oil does not nourish? Didn’t we learn» in a mishna: «One who vows that nourishment» is forbidden to him «is permitted» to eat «water and salt,» as they are not considered nourishment. «And we discussed this» halakha: By inference, «water and salt are not considered nourishment, but all» other edible «items are considered nourishment.»

segments.he: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמְרִי אֵין מְבָרְכִין ״בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת״ אֶלָּא בַּחֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִין בִּלְבַד. וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּאוֹמֵר ״כׇּל הַזָּן עָלַי״.
segments.en: «Let us say that this is a conclusive refutation of Rav and Shmuel, who said: One only recites: Who creates various kinds of nourishment, over the five species» of grain «alone,» as they alone are considered nourishing. «And Rav Huna said» as a solution that this mishna referred to a case «where» he vows «and says: Anything that nourishes» is prohibited «to me.» That formula includes anything that is at all nourishing and therefore only water and salt are excluded. Olive oil is not excluded.

segments.he: אַלְמָא מִשְׁחָא זָיֵין! אֶלָּא, חַמְרָא סָעֵיד, וּמִשְׁחָא לָא סָעֵיד. וְחַמְרָא מִי סָעֵיד? וְהָא רָבָא הֲוָה שָׁתֵי חַמְרָא כׇּל מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִסְחָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנִגְרְרֵיהּ לְלִבֵּיהּ וְנֵיכוֹל מַצָּה טְפֵי? טוּבָא — גָּרֵיר, פּוּרְתָּא — סָעֵיד.
segments.en: «Apparently, oil nourishes. Rather,» there is another distinction between wine and oil: «Wine satisfies, oil does not satisfy.» Wine not only nourishes, but it is also filling. The Gemara asks: «And does wine satisfy? Wouldn’t Rava drink wine all» day on «the eve of Passover in order to stimulate his heart,» i.e., whet his appetite «so that he might eat more matza» at the seder? Wine does not satisfy, it whets the appetite. The Gemara answers: «A lot» of wine «stimulates, a little satisfies.»

segments.he: וּמִי סָעֵיד כְּלָל?! וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְיַיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד וְגוֹ׳״ — נַהֲמָא הוּא דְּסָעֵיד חַמְרָא לָא סָעֵיד! אֶלָּא, חַמְרָא אִית בֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי: סָעֵיד וּמְשַׂמַּח. נַהֲמָא מִסְעָד סָעֵיד, שַׂמּוֹחֵי לָא מְשַׂמַּח.
segments.en: Again, the Gemara asks: «Does» wine «satisfy at all? Isn’t it written: “Wine gladdens the heart of man,» making the face brighter than oil, «and bread fills man’s heart”» (Psalms 104:15); «bread is that which satisfies, wine does not satisfy. Rather,» this verse is not a proof; «wine has two» advantages, «it satisfies and gladdens. Bread,» however, «satisfies but does not gladden.»

segments.he: אִי הָכִי נְבָרֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת! לָא קָבְעִי אִינָשֵׁי סְעוֹדְתַּיְיהוּ עִלָּוֵיהּ.
segments.en: Since wine possesses all of these virtues, the Gemara asks: «If so, let us recite» the «three blessings» of Grace after Meals «over it» after drinking, just as we do after eating bread. The Gemara answers: «People do not base their meals on» wine.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא: אִי קָבַע עִלָּוֵיהּ סְעוֹדְתֵּיהּ מַאי? אָמַר לֵיהּ: לִכְשֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר אִי הָוֵי קְבִיעוּתָא. הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא בָּטְלָה דַּעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כׇּל אָדָם.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rava: If one based his meal on it, what is the» ruling? Must he recite the Grace after Meals as he does after bread? He replied: «When Elijah comes and says whether» or not «it can serve as the basis» for a meal, this will be resolved. «Nevertheless, now,» until then, «his intention is» rendered «irrelevant by» the opinions of «all other men» and he is not required to recite the complete Grace after Meals.

moves.summary: Answers the previous unit's question: oil has no blessing of its own because none can be formulated.
moves.about: why olive oil, though improved like wine, has no blessing of its own — no suitable formula is available

moves.summary: Floats a candidate formula: Who creates fruit of the olive.
Knocks it down: the fruit itself is what is called olive.
A formula is available after all — Who creates fruit of the olive tree.
moves.about: whether a formula really is unavailable — בורא פרי עץ זית would parallel the blessing over wine

moves.summary: Mar Zutra: wine nourishes, oil does not.
moves.about: the real distinction — wine nourishes and oil does not

moves.summary: Objects from the mishna on one who vows against nourishment.
moves.about: whether oil nourishes — the mishna implies everything but water and salt counts as nourishment

moves.summary: Only water and salt are excluded, so everything else counts as nourishment.
moves.about: brings the mishna that one who vows against nourishment may still have water and salt

moves.summary: Proposes that this refutes Rav and Shmuel, who limit מזונות to the five species.
moves.about: whether only the five species of grain count as מזון, against the mishna's implication that everything but water and salt does

moves.summary: Rav Huna narrows the mishna to a vow phrased כל הזן עלי.
moves.about: the mishna's case is one who vowed in the wording כל הזן עלי, which sweeps in whatever nourishes

moves.summary: Even so, oil is shown to nourish — so Mar Zutra's distinction fails.
moves.about: even on Rav Huna's reading only water and salt are excluded, so oil does nourish

moves.cueHe: אלא, חמרא סעיד, ומשחא לא סעיד
moves.summary: Restates the distinction: wine satisfies, oil does not.
moves.about: the distinction is restated — wine satisfies and oil does not

moves.cueHe: וחמרא מי סעיד? והא רבא הוה שתי חמרא
moves.summary: Rava drank wine on Passover eve to whet his appetite — so wine does not satisfy.
moves.about: whether wine satisfies at all, given that Rava drank it to whet his appetite

moves.summary: A lot of wine stimulates, a little satisfies.
moves.about: a lot of wine stimulates the appetite while a little satisfies

moves.summary: The verse assigns satisfying to bread and only gladdening to wine.
moves.about: the verse assigns satisfying to bread and only gladdening to wine, against the claim that wine satisfies

moves.summary: Wine has both properties; bread satisfies without gladdening.
moves.about: wine has both properties — it satisfies and gladdens — while bread satisfies without gladdening

moves.cueHe: אי הכי נבריך עליה שלש ברכות
moves.summary: Then wine should take the three blessings of Grace after Meals.
moves.about: if wine really satisfies, the three blessings of Grace after Meals should be recited over it

moves.summary: People do not base their meals on wine.
moves.about: people do not base their meals on wine, so it does not take the full Grace after Meals

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב נחמן בר יצחק לרבא
moves.summary: And if someone did base his meal on wine?
moves.about: what the ruling is if a person did base his meal on wine

moves.summary: That awaits Elijah; meanwhile his intention is nullified by the practice of all other men.
moves.about: whether an individual's basing his meal on wine counts as קביעות — deferred until Elijah rules, and meanwhile his intention is nullified by the practice of all other men
